§9.1.2 Chart With a Printed Data Grid

📄 Page rule — applied from the page alone

tables-chart-with-a-printed-data-grid · tables charts orientation

✅ Normative

When a chart prints its data grid beside or beneath the canvas, the output MUST render that grid exactly as printed — same orientation, same headers, same row order — and MUST NOT render any other table for the chart.

Some charts print their numbers as a small grid next to the canvas: a bar chart with bucket-columns × metric-rows underneath, for example. That printed grid is often transposed relative to the [Category, Value] shape a chart is usually reasoned about in.

Printed under the bar chart:            Transposed reconstruction — non-conforming:
| Metric   | $0–1k | $1k–5k | $5k+ |    | Bucket | Avg Premium |
| Avg Prem | 412   | 388    | 351  |    | $0–1k  | 412         |
                                        | $1k–5k | 388         |

Requirements

  • The table representing the chart MUST open with <table data-source="chart">, including when its values come from the printed grid.
  • The grid MUST be transcribed in its printed orientation. Metrics that run across the top stay across the top.
  • The grid MUST NOT be transposed, and its rows and columns MUST NOT be reordered into a more natural shape.
  • The output MUST NOT add a second, reconstructed version alongside it. One grid is printed; one grid is rendered.
  • Values MUST NOT be re-keyed off the chart canvas — bars, points and axis ticks are not the source. Only what is printed as text in the grid counts.

A transposed version is non-conforming even when it reads better, in the same way that rewriting a cell's text is non-conforming.

Why as printed

This is the verbatim posture the whole protocol takes: transcribe what is on the page, do not improve it (see Cell Text Fidelity§9.6.3, Accounting Number Formats§9.6.1). A second reconstructed copy also creates the duplication described in Duplicated Tables§9.2.4 and Titles Banners Captions§9.7.3 — two tables where the page printed one (never invent).

✅ Sample — two charts with their grids beneath

Each chart prints a four-row grid under its bars — one row per series, one column per quarter, with the year as a spanning row between the quarters and the values. The grid is the rendering; the bars are not re-keyed.
